speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Prime Minister (a) what is the current adoption rate of PayNow and PayNow Corporate; (b) whether the adoption rate has met the Government's target; (c) what is the current adoption rate of QR code payment in Singapore, especially at hawker centres; and (d) what is the plan to further push the adoption rate of cashless transactions in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This represents approximately half of the total number of UENs issued to active businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The numbers are also on an upward trend.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Two years ago, when PayNow was launched, there were about 150,000 transactions totaling about S$24 million in the first month of operations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng also asked about the adoption of quick response (QR) code payments.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: QR codes are a low-cost and effective way for merchants to receive e-payments from their customers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In September 2018, we collaborated with the industry to launch SGQR, our national QR code that consolidated the various QRs of international and domestic payment schemes into a single unified interface.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This represents a penetration rate of about 20% of all retail acceptance points.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: So, there is a lot more work to do.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Specifically on hawker centres, Enterprise Singapore has collaborated with the Network for Electronic Transfers (NETS) to deploy a unified e-payment solution at small food businesses since December 2018.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: E-payments usage at these stalls is gradually increasing and four out of five e-payment transactions are via SGQR.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: While the volume of e-payments is still low compared to cash, we expect it to grow.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: E-payments are convenient to use at hawker stalls and payment operators are looking into ways to make it even more convenient for hawkers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We made a deliberate decision not to have one player dominate the landscape and roll out very quickly where you end up dominating and monopolising the landscape.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Instead, we put in place the backbone infrastructure, so that multiple providers can compete and innovate to increase consumer choice, while encouraging interoperability.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: As a result, Singaporeans can now make e-payments in multiple ways which are simple, swift and secure.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Singaporeans are making more contactless payments using credit and debit cards, such as Apple Pay and Google Pay.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: They can use QR payments via e-wallets and also use PayNow.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: As a result, the ratio of cash and cheque usage relative to e-payments has decreased significantly over time.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We will continue to enhance the e-payments infrastructure for Singaporeans from all walks to experience convenient and low-cost e-payments.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: We note that PayNow is more popular amongst individuals, compared to the corporates and companies, as per the figures given by the Minister.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: So, would the Minister consider asking the banks to promote PayNow Corporate more before they start changing the charges for cheques?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Some local banks now charge 75 cents per cheque right from the first cheque instead of the first 30 cheques for free previously.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: This could be a bit premature because a lot of companies, like the Minister said, half the companies, are still not using PayNow Corporate.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For PayNow Corporate, the take-up is not so bad – as I mentioned earlier, it is now half of the UENs – considering that it was launched only in August 2018, a year ago.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think having this carrot-and-stick, push-and-pull approach, we will continue to see higher take-up of PayNow Corporate.
